sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's data-center buildout is a durable driver as hyperscalers (Google, AWS) expand in Batam and Jakarta, boosting local infrastructure plays like TRON and MLPT.
Global semiconductor cycle upswing, led by memory (MU, WDC) and AI chips, directly lifts Indonesia's tech ecosystem via supply-chain linkages and investor sentiment.
Government push for digitalization (Pindar 2025, e-commerce growth) creates structural demand for local tech services, benefiting firms like GPSO and NBIS in payments and logistics.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector surged on US semiconductor strength (MU, WDC up 12%+) and local AI/data-center plays (TRON +27%, MLPT +25%), signaling a risk-on rotation into high-beta names. Position into TRON and MLPT for domestic AI infrastructure exposure, as US chip momentum supports global sentiment and Indonesia's digital economy narrative accelerates.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's mandated biodiesel blending (B35) and upcoming B40 target create durable demand for palm-oil-based renewable fuels, directly benefiting domestic producers like ARKO and TPIA.
Government push for 23% renewable energy mix by 2025, though delayed, drives structural investment in geothermal and solar, favoring local EPC players like CDIA and BREN.
Global decarbonization trends and US Inflation Reduction Act spillovers support Indonesia's nickel-based battery supply chain, but export-dependent names face geopolitical and price volatility risks.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables rally, led by ARKO (+18%) and CDIA (+9%), signals growing domestic conviction in the energy transition, but US-listed names like PLUG (+6.6%) add volatility. Watch for policy catalysts from the new administration and local currency tailwinds; the sector's +3.24% ID outperformance vs +0.26% US suggests a tactical entry point for Indonesia-focused investors, but remain selective on liquidity and regulatory clarity.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class consumption in Indonesia drives demand for branded FMCG and protein products, supported by urbanization and digital penetration.
Government policies promoting food self-sufficiency and local sourcing benefit domestic producers like AGAR and BEEF, reducing import dependency.
Formal retail expansion and e-commerce growth in Indonesia create distribution advantages for FMCG players with strong brand equity and rural reach.
sectors.ai: Indonesia consumer/FMCG outperformed (+0.81% ID) vs US (-0.43%), with strong gains in AGAR, BEEF, COCO, and others signaling resilient domestic demand. Focus on companies with pricing power and local supply chains to capture structural consumption growth, as global headwinds remain muted.

The shift toward public-private partnerships (PPP) for infrastructure financing reduces fiscal burden and opens recurring revenue streams for toll road operators like SULI and NRCA.
